We need propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: steps forward: 1) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). 2) Doebner modification to form α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid. 3) sulfonamide formation from amine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus retrosynthetic steps (reverse) would be:

Target -> disconnect amide bond: break C(=O)N linking the unsaturated chain to aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). So precursor 1: the acid (α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid) Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1? Wait the amide is C(=O)N attached to aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). The amide carbonyl is part of the unsaturated chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-aryl. So retro step: remove amide, giving acid: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1? Actually the acid would be the α,β-unsaturated acid: /C=C/ C(=O)OH attached to aromatic ring? The unsaturated acid attached to aromatic ring via the double bond? The structure: ...c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the aromatic ring c2 has a side chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-aryl. So the acid precursor would be same but with COOH instead of CONH-aryl. So precursor A: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2)cc1 (the α,β-unsaturated acid). Then second step: that acid derived from Doebner modification of aromatic aldehyde (the same aromatic ring with aldehyde) plus malonic acid to give the α,β-unsaturated acid. So precursor B: aromatic aldehyde: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(CHO)cc2)cc1 (i.e., same core but aldehyde). Third step: sulfonamide formation: the sulfonamide group NS(=O)(=O) attached to aromatic ring (first phenyl). That came from reaction of an amine (aniline) with sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-aryl). So precursor C: the amine: Cc1ccc(NH2)cc1 (p-toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride: ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(??)?? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to second phenyl ring (the one bearing the side chain). So sulfonyl chloride: ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(??)?? The second phenyl has the side chain (aldehyde). So sulfonyl chloride: ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(CHO)cc2. So overall route:

Step1 (retro): amide formation -> precursors: α,β-unsaturated acid (A) + aniline (c3ccccc3N). Step2 (retro): Doebner modification -> precursors: aromatic aldehyde (B) + malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). Step3 (retro): sulfonamide formation -> precursors: p-toluidine (C) + sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-aryl with aldehyde) (D). D is derived from aldehyde B? Actually B is the aldehyde attached to phenyl ring that will become sulfonyl chloride after chlorination? Wait sulfonyl chloride is attached to aromatic ring (the second phenyl). In target, the sulfonyl group is attached to the first phenyl (tolyl) via nitrogen, and the sulfonyl group is attached to second phenyl (the one with side chain). So sulfonyl chloride precursor is ClSO2-aryl where aryl is the second phenyl with aldehyde (or later side chain). So we can get that sulfonyl chloride from the aldehyde B by converting aldehyde to sulfonyl chloride? Not typical. But we can treat sulfonyl chloride as separate reagent, not derived from target. So we can propose using commercially available sulfonyl chloride (p-tolyl-sulfonyl chloride? Actually we need sulfonyl chloride of second phenyl). Could be 4-(formyl)phenylsulfonyl chloride. That may be available.

Thus route: 1) Couple acid (A) with aniline (c3ccccc3N) to give amide. 2) Synthesize acid A via Doebner from aldehyde B and malonic acid. 3) Synthesize aldehyde B via sulfonamide formation between p-toluidine and sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-aryl with aldehyde). Wait sulfonamide formation attaches sulfonyl group to amine, giving NSO2-aryl. So we need p-toluidine (C) + sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-aryl with aldehyde) to give sulfonamide intermediate (the core before side chain). That intermediate is exactly the target without side chain? Actually after sulfonamide formation we have Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)Ar)cc1 where Ar is phenyl with aldehyde. That's the precursor for Doebner.

Thus we have 3 steps.

Now we need to produce JSON route with 3 reaction nodes.

We need template IDs for each reaction. We can search for templates matching functional groups.

Step 1: amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine). Use functional_groups_broken: aliphatic carboxylic acid, functional_groups_formed: amide. Let's search again with correct functional group names: "aliphatic carboxylic acid". Already used earlier but got results. We need a template ID from results. The search returned list with reaction_id etc but not template_id field. It includes 'template_hash' and 'retro_smarts_template'. We need template_id (maybe same as reaction_id?). The tool expects template_id string. In examples they use numeric IDs. Probably we can use reaction_id as template_id. We'll pick first result reaction_id 401931 for amide formation? That template seems to involve amide formation with double bond? Not sure. But we can use it.

Step2: Doebner modification: functional_groups_broken: aldehyde, malonic acid? The transformation forms C-C double bond and carboxylic acid. We need template that breaks aldehyde and forms C-C double bond. Let's search functional_groups_broken ["aldehydes"] functional_groups_formed ["C-C double bonds"].
